clue.text: Complain audibly, except where drinks are served

indicators.note: audibly means as heard, so the word for complaining is taken by its sound and respelt

parts.note: to whine is to complain; heard, it is the same as the drink
bar means except, as in 'all bar one'

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles loudly about everything except the pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A wine bar is an establishment serving wine and other drinks, so it is a place where drinks are served.

clue.text: Relish having gone straight?

wordplay.note: someone now straight used to be bisexual: read as three words, past tense, article and the short form of bisexual

explanation.surface: A wry remark about enjoying life after giving up crime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gone straight' suggests reforming from crime; here it means turning heterosexual, so the person once was a bi, read as three words.
explanation.definitionFit: Wasabi is a pungent green Japanese condiment, so it is a relish served alongside sushi.

clue.text: In a bad way upon eating lots of Asian food

indicators.note: in a bad way means in poor shape, so the short word that follows is put out of order
eating means taking inside, so the scrambled word swallows the abundance word

parts.note: these letters rearranged
oodles means lots

explanation.surface: Someone feeling unwell after gorging on plenty of Asian dishes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In a bad way' reads as the state of the diner, but it scrambles the next word, which then swallows the abundance word.
explanation.definitionFit: Noodle soup, broth with noodles such as ramen or pho, is a staple dish of East and Southeast Asia.

clue.text: Yet the barn could be better for her

definitions.text: Yet the barn could be better for her

indicators.note: could be suggests the letters might become something else once rearranged

parts.note: these letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A barn would still be an improvement for a caged bird.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: a hen kept in a cage would be better off barn-raised.
explanation.definitionFit: A battery hen is a laying chicken kept in a small cage, so even a barn would be a welfare improvement.

clue.text: Wiped out old section of paper as editor

indicators.note: a section of is a portion cut from something, so the letters run across the following words

parts.note: found running across the three words

explanation.surface: An editor deletes an outdated part of a newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old' warns that this is an archaic spelling, of razed or erased.
explanation.definitionFit: Rased is an old spelling meaning erased or razed, both senses of something destroyed or removed.

clue.text: Be an agitator around mid-April and put one's foot in it

definitions.note: a cryptic paraphrase: the answer is the thing you put your foot in

indicators.note: around says the phrase for agitating wraps about the next letter

parts.note: to stir up is to agitate trouble

indicators.note: mid asks for the central letter only of the month that follows

parts.note: the middle letter of the five-letter month

explanation.surface: A troublemaker stirs things up in spring and commits a gaffe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put one's foot in it' wants to mean blunder; read literally it describes what a rider does with the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A stirrup is the metal loop hanging from a saddle into which a rider literally places a foot.

clue.text: Farcical friend is back in seconds

indicators.note: back means going the other way, so the word for friend is read backwards
in puts the reversed friend inside a pair of second abbreviations

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for second, here doubled
a pal is a friend
a tick is a second, a moment

explanation.surface: A buddy is back in a moment, behaving clownishly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seconds' works hard: two S abbreviations surround the reversed friend, and TICK, another word for a second, follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Slapstick is boisterous physical comedy, so as a modifier it describes farcical humour.

clue.text: Rebecca's chasing one goat

indicators.note: chasing means coming behind, so the name is placed after the numeral

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one
Bex is a short form of Rebecca

explanation.surface: Rebecca chases a single goat.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's means 'is'; the pet name Bex is spelt with an X.
explanation.definitionFit: The ibex is a wild mountain goat of the Alps and Asia with long curved horns.

clue.text: Royal protection for one charged in a particular area

indicators.note: protection for means guarding by surrounding, so the royal word wraps the charged particle

parts.note: regal means royal
an ion is an electrically charged particle

explanation.surface: Royal bodyguards for someone charged with a crime in a certain district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one charged' suggests someone accused; it is a particle with an electric charge.
explanation.definitionFit: Regional describes something belonging to or occurring within one district, a specific part of a country.

clue.text: Hats from Melton Mowbray?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: flat-topped hats with a turned-up brim
second meaning: the famous savoury pastries of that town

explanation.walkthrough: Melton Mowbray is a Leicestershire market town famous for its meat pastries; the question mark marks them as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: The name is shared by a hat style whose crown resembles the pastry and the meat-filled baked goods themselves.

clue.text: Film branch fire

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to film a scene
second meaning: a new growth on a plant
third meaning: to fire a gun

explanation.walkthrough: Three separate meanings of one word sit side by side; the surface suggests burning a branch on film.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers recording on camera, a young plant stem, and discharging a weapon, matching all three senses.

clue.text: Perhaps vulture's nemesis pursuing strategic ends

indicators.note: pursuing means coming after, so the nemesis word follows the other piece
ends asks for just the first and final letters of the preceding word

parts.note: the outside letters of the word
Nemesis was the Greek goddess of retribution, an avenger

explanation.surface: A vulture's deadly enemy hunting with strategic aims.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', joining definition to wordplay; 'Perhaps' marks the vulture as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A vulture is a classic example of a carrion-eating bird, the kind of animal that feeds on carcasses.

clue.text: Rubbish race that's not so hairy

parts.note: balder is less hairy
a dash is a short race, a sprint

explanation.surface: A dismissive comment about a race for those with less hair.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay pieces come in reverse order from the clue: the 'not so hairy' piece goes first.
explanation.definitionFit: Balderdash is nonsense talk, so it is a synonym for rubbish in the sense of foolish words.

clue.text: See 2
Like New York? Going up with friend to reserve hotel, doing it at different times

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase for the noun's state

parts.note: as means like

indicators.note: going up in a down clue means reading from the bottom, so the city's abbreviation runs backwards

parts.note: the standard abbreviation

indicators.note: to reserve means to keep inside, so the friend word holds the hotel letter

parts.note: a crony is a close friend
H is Hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Planning a New York trip with a friend who books the hotel, but on separate schedules.
explanation.definitionFit: Asynchrony is the state of events not occurring together, of things happening out of step in time.

clue.text: Perjury before tea isn't wrong when dead?

indicators.note: wrong means incorrectly arranged, so the letters of the preceding pair of words are rearranged

parts.note: perjury is lying under oath
these letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A puzzled question whether telling lies before tea stops being wrong once you have died.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the definition as an example: being displayed in this way happens only when dead.
explanation.definitionFit: A dead dignitary's body is displayed publicly before burial, which is the ceremony named by the answer.

clue.text: New ground connection that almost didn't make it

parts.note: N is the abbreviation for new
earthing is the electrical connection to ground

explanation.surface: A fresh electrical earth wire was very nearly not fitted.
explanation.walkthrough: In British usage an electrical ground is called earth, and connecting to it is earthing.
explanation.definitionFit: A near thing is a narrow escape, something that only just succeeded or was barely avoided.

clue.text: Where students are affected, when overwhelmed by responsibility

indicators.note: overwhelmed by means swamped and surrounded, so the affected word sits inside the duty word

parts.note: an onus is a duty or responsibility
camp means affected, theatrical

explanation.surface: Students are emotionally affected when swamped by responsibilities.
explanation.definitionFit: Students living or studying at a university are located within its grounds, the campus.

clue.text: One's smart to have packed underwear

parts.note: a bra is an undergarment
packed means put in a box

explanation.surface: A clever traveller remembers to pack their underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One's smart' reads as a person who is smart; a brainbox is British slang for a very clever person.
explanation.definitionFit: A brainbox is an informal term for a highly intelligent person, someone clever and bright.

clue.text: Kissing when hugging wild raver is stressful

indicators.note: wild means out of control, so the partygoer's letters are scrambled
hugging means wrapping arms around, so the kissing word encloses the other letters

parts.note: necking is kissing and cuddling
the partygoer's letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Snogging while embracing an out-of-control partygoer is a nerve-wracking experience.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that strains the nerves causes anxiety, so the compound adjective is a synonym for stressful.

clue.text: Skilful craftsman's hinges

indicators.note: the apostrophe s stands for has, so the phrase has the solution within it

parts.note: found running across the two words

explanation.surface: A skilled craftsman's hinges.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is read as 'has': the craftsman phrase has the answer inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Fulcra, plural of fulcrum, are pivot points on which levers turn, which is what a hinge provides.

clue.text: James undressed, got into bed and smiled

indicators.note: undressed means stripped of outer clothing, so the name loses its outermost letters
got into means entered, so the stripped name goes inside the sleeping place

parts.note: taken as written
the name without its first and last letters

explanation.surface: James stripped off, climbed into bed and grinned.
explanation.definitionFit: To beam is to give a broad happy grin, so beamed is a synonym for smiled widely.

clue.text: Making contents similar

indicators.note: contents means what is inside, so only the interior letters of the word are kept

parts.note: the word without its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Producing contents that resemble each other.
explanation.definitionFit: Akin is an adjective meaning of the same kind, closely related, which is a synonym for similar.

clue.text: Ask the drunk by the river for a place to eat

indicators.note: drunk suggests staggering and disordered, so the preceding letters are jumbled

parts.note: these letters rearranged
the Ouse is a river in England, a crossword staple

explanation.surface: Asking a drunk by the river where you might find somewhere to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the' does double duty in the fodder; the Ouse is one of several English rivers by that name.
explanation.definitionFit: A steakhouse is a restaurant specialising in grilled beef, so it is a place where one dines.

clue.text: Void in 28 Debussy ballet

indicators.note: the cross-referenced answer means heading upwards, so in a down entry the letters read from the bottom
in says the solution lies inside the words that follow

parts.note: found running across the two words

explanation.surface: An empty space in a Debussy ballet.
explanation.walkthrough: 28 refers to the answer at 28 across, which tells you the hidden letters go upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: An abyss is a bottomless chasm, so it is a void, an immense empty depth.

clue.text: Fruit for bird

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the green-fleshed fruit with brown furry skin
second meaning: the flightless bird of New Zealand

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests food for a bird; the two nouns are separate meanings of the same word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a Chinese gooseberry, the fruit, and New Zealand's national flightless bird.

clue.text: Bar with legal liability finally gets promotion

parts.note: a pub is a bar
licit means lawful

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter only of the word before it

parts.note: the word's last letter

explanation.surface: A pub with legal liability ends up getting promoted.
explanation.definitionFit: Publicity is the attention or advertising that promotes something, so it is a synonym for promotion.

clue.text: Clutching a small volume, chairman turns philosopher

indicators.note: turns means flips round, so the chairman's name is read backwards
clutching means holding tightly, so the leader's name encloses the measure

parts.note: Chairman Mao, the Chinese communist leader
a cubic centimetre, cc, is a small volume

explanation.surface: A chairman holding a slim book turns into a philosopher.
explanation.definitionFit: William of Occam was a medieval English friar and thinker, known for the principle called Occam's razor.

clue.text: Tax easing off, but not as explicit communication

indicators.note: off means gone bad or out of order, so the remaining letters are rearranged
not as is read as minus the letter a, plural, so every such letter is dropped

parts.note: the two words taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A tax cut is off, but not as clearly stated as hoped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as' is not a word to drop: it is the plural of the letter A, so both As go before the rest is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Sexting is sending sexually explicit messages by phone, a form of communication that is explicit.

clue.text: Extremely sick boy at last might be here, getting up

indicators.note: extremely points to the extreme, outermost letters of the next word

parts.note: the first and last letters

indicators.note: at last asks for only the final letter of the word before

parts.note: the last letter
a sick boy might be in a hospital ward

explanation.surface: A very ill youngster might be found here, rising from bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'might be here' points back at the sick boy: the place a patient would be.
explanation.definitionFit: Skyward means towards the sky, upwards, so it describes something rising or going up.
